atlas_home_region_card.compact: The 1970s album-rock backbone: canonical LPs, FM-radio standards, guitar bands, and songs that became shared rock memory.
atlas_home_region_card.standard: It became the default rock reference library for several generations: riffs, album covers, long songs, stadium scale, road-trip radio, and deep-cut familiarity.
atlas_home_region_card.deep: The 1970s album-rock backbone: canonical LPs, FM-radio standards, guitar bands, and songs that became shared rock memory. It became the default rock reference library for several generations: riffs, album covers, long songs, stadium scale, road-trip radio, and deep-cut familiarity.

region_scene_page.compact: Classic rock is an afterlife as much as an era.
region_scene_page.standard: Classic rock is an afterlife as much as an era. The Who's Won't Get Fooled Again, Led Zeppelin's Kashmir, Bob Seger's Night Moves, and Queen's We Will Rock You give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: Classic rock is an afterlife as much as an era. The lane is broad but not random; its center is the album-rock listening habit, where songs and LPs become durable objects together. The Who's Won't Get Fooled Again, Led Zeppelin's Kashmir, Bob Seger's Night Moves, and Queen's We Will Rock You give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.

mission_detail_history_module.compact: What this route tests: The 1970s album-rock backbone: canonical LPs, FM-radio standards, guitar bands, and songs that became shared rock memory.
mission_detail_history_module.standard: Classic rock is an afterlife as much as an era. Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd, Fleetwood Mac, Eagles, Creedence, Queen, and related artists were made durable through albums, touring, radio repetition, and later canon-building. It helps place this road in a broader music-history context.
mission_detail_history_module.deep: Classic rock is an afterlife as much as an era. Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd, Fleetwood Mac, Eagles, Creedence, Queen, and related artists were made durable through albums, touring, radio repetition, and later canon-building. It became the default rock reference library for several generations: riffs, album covers, long songs, stadium scale, road-trip radio, and deep-cut familiarity.
